name: Cuba

findings.summary: ETECSA, Cuba's sole state telecom and internet provider, names Huawei, ZTE and TP-Link as its main technology suppliers per its own magazine; OONI's 2017 measurements found Huawei access points in Cuba's internet infrastructure.

sources.publisher: Institute for War and Peace Reporting (republished by ecoi.net)

findings.analyst_inference: Two opened sources on different hosts (IWPR S3, OONI S2 technical measurement) both place Huawei equipment in ETECSA's network; neither identifies which RAN/core elements Huawei or ZTE supply, so share and layer depth are unknown. The supplier list traces to ETECSA's corporate magazine (S4) relayed by IWPR. Tier 5 because the equipment is in operational use; still_current not confirmed for 2026. A 'possible' Huawei web-filtering product (Qurium) is unconfirmed and not coded.

findings.summary: ETECSA launched a home fibre broadband pilot in Old Havana run with Huawei, letting residents and small businesses order fixed internet connections for the first time.
findings.analyst_inference: Pre-2020 pilot; whether it was scaled up to the later Nauta Hogar service on Huawei gear was not confirmed, so still_current is null. Both wire stories relay the same ETECSA/state-media announcement and are not S1/S2, so the corroboration rule is not met.

findings.local_actor: Telecomunicaciones Gran Caribe (Telecom Venezuela 60% / Transbit, Cuba)
findings.summary: The ALBA-1 submarine cable, 1,860 km from Siboney (Santiago de Cuba) to La Guaira with a Jamaica branch, was completed in 2012 and carried traffic from January 2013; final cost about US$70m.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the equipment vendor was Alcatel-Lucent's Chinese joint-venture subsidiary Alcatel-Lucent Shanghai Bell (now Nokia Shanghai Bell), so firmware/update control sits between a European parent and a PRC state-held JV; not resolved here. Owner-operator is a Venezuelan-Cuban state JV. Pre-2020 and still_current unconfirmed, though ALBA-1 is widely reported as Cuba's main international link. Not an HMN Tech cable. NBC seen in search results only. Audit 2026-10-25: newer information - CircleID (2013-01-24): latency analysis showed some Cuban international traffic moving from satellite to cable in January 2013; ETECSA had not confirmed it.

findings.controller: Universidad de La Habana (Faculty of Mathematics and Computing)
findings.local_actor: Unión de Informáticos de Cuba / Ministerio de Comunicaciones
findings.summary: University of Havana researchers presented CecilIA, a Cuban-Spanish language model built on the existing Salamandra model and trained on a roughly 207 GB local corpus including literature, the Official Gazette and speeches.

sources.publisher: Ministerio de Comunicaciones de Cuba (republishing UIC)

findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 2 as a research presentation with no evidence of deployment. Salamandra is assumed to be the Barcelona Supercomputing Center's open model (Spain, hence base_model_pole third); the page does not name its developer. Date inferred from the Cibersociedad 2025 congress (image filename suggests 7 October 2025). Single government page; state-affiliated framing possible.

facilities.null_reason: no large data-centre or AI-campus project since 2023 found in 2 searches; Chinese donations surfaced were for power-grid and telecom solar backup, not data centres

silicon.null_reason: comprehensive US embargo (global layer); no accelerator deployment (Nvidia or Ascend) surfaced in searches

applications.null_reason: reporting on police video surveillance (e.g. Varadero) names no vendor; Huawei web-filtering product reported only as 'possible'

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced; search budget spent on other layers

corrections.note: Weekly audit 2026-10-25: 2 selected finding(s) source-checked by independent checkers; corrections from pages the checkers read (dates, summaries, still_current, newer information, added opened sources) and spec-required recoding.

research_gaps: Which vendor supplies ETECSA's 3G/4G RAN and core (Huawei vs ZTE share)? Seek ETECSA tender records or vendor filings.
Is Huawei or ZTE equipment used for ETECSA's DPI/web filtering? Qurium's report claimed only a 'possible' Huawei product; obtain and assess it.
Did Cuba and China sign telecom/AI instruments at the September 2025 meeting with MIIT minister Li Lecheng (DPL News reported a working meeting, no signed instrument)?
Status of the 2019 Hebei-Camagüey university AI centre agreement (tier 1, academic) — not coded.
Is ALBA-1 still Cuba's primary international link, and who supplies upgrades (Nokia Shanghai Bell)? Any newer cable (e.g. PRC-built) planned?
Reported PRC signals/intelligence facilities in Cuba were deliberately not coded: not stack adoption without network/facility sourcing.
Vendor of police video-surveillance cameras in Havana and Varadero (Hikvision/Dahua?) is unverified.
